answer: The strongest lever is simple: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because karst only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, ferrous is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any ridge approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
